questions.q: What is Newton's second law of motion defined as in terms of momentum?
a: The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the net external force acting on it and takes place in the direction in which the force acts.
Force is equal to mass multiplied by velocity.
The momentum of an isolated system remains constant.
Action and reaction forces are equal and opposite.

questions.q: A constant force of 20 N acts on a body of mass 4.0 kg initially at rest. What is the momentum of the body after 3.0 s?
A block of mass 5.0 kg is pulled up a frictionless incline of 30 degrees to the horizontal by a parallel force of 40 N. What is the acceleration of the block? (g = 9.81 m s⁻²)
Which of the following represents the unit of linear momentum in SI base units?

What is the physical principle underlying the recoil velocity of a gun when fired?
Two masses M1 = 3.0 kg and M2 = 2.0 kg are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth frictionless pulley. What is the acceleration of the system? (g = 9.81 m s⁻²)
What is meant by an inelastic collision?
a: A collision in which linear momentum is not conserved
A collision in which kinetic energy is conserved but momentum is not
A collision in which kinetic energy is not conserved, though total linear momentum is conserved
A collision where objects permanently shatter into dust

questions.q: A force-time graph shows a force rising linearly from 0 to 50 N in 2.0 s and then remaining constant at 50 N for another 3.0 s. What is the total impulse delivered to the object over the 5.0 s interval?
A 1000 kg car traveling at 20 m s⁻¹ collides with a stationary wall and comes to rest in 0.20 s. What is the average magnitude of the force exerted on the car by the wall?
Which statement best describes Newton's third law of motion?
a: If a body is acted upon by a balanced force, it remains at rest or in uniform motion.
The net force on an object is proportional to its rate of change of momentum.
Forces always occur in pairs; if body A exerts a force on body B, body B exerts an equal and opposite force on body A of the exact same type.
Action and reaction forces cancel each other out because they act on the same body.

questions.q: A box of mass 10 kg is dragged across a rough horizontal floor with a constant velocity by a horizontal force of 30 N. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the box and the floor? (g = 9.81 m s⁻²)
A shell of mass 2.0 kg is fired horizontally from a stationary cannon of mass 200 kg with a muzzle velocity of 300 m s⁻¹. What is the recoil velocity of the cannon?
What is the definition of impulse in terms of force and time?
a: The product of force and distance
The rate of change of force
The product of the net force and the time interval during which it acts
The kinetic energy imparted per unit time

questions.q: A ball of mass 0.5 kg strikes a vertical wall horizontally with a speed of 10 m s⁻¹ and rebounds along its original path with a speed of 8.0 m s⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the impulse received by the ball?
In an elastic collision between two bodies in one dimension, which of the following quantities is conserved?
a: Both total linear momentum and total kinetic energy
Total momentum only, while kinetic energy is lost
Total kinetic energy only, while momentum changes

questions.q: A block of mass 4.0 kg rests on a rough horizontal table. The coefficient of static friction is 0.40. What is the minimum horizontal force required to start the block moving? (g = 9.81 m s⁻²)
A 2.0 kg trolley moving at 3.0 m s⁻¹ collides head-on with a stationary 1.0 kg trolley. After the collision, they stick together. What is their common speed?
Which of the following scenarios demonstrates Newton's first law of motion?
a: A rocket accelerating in deep space
A book resting on a table experiencing a normal contact force equal to its weight
A ball accelerating as it falls freely under gravity
A spaceship drifting through outer space at constant velocity with engines shut down

questions.q: A particle of mass m moving with velocity u undergoes an elastic head-on collision with an identical stationary particle. What are their velocities after the collision?
a: First particle stops, second particle moves with velocity u
Both particles move with velocity u / 2
First particle rebounds with -u, second stays at rest
Both particles move in opposite directions at u

questions.q: A constant force accelerates a 500 g mass from rest to a speed of 10 m s⁻¹ in 2.0 s. What is the magnitude of the force?
What is the main reason why seatbelts and airbags save lives during a vehicle collision according to momentum principles?
a: They increase the total momentum change of the passenger.
They decrease the final velocity of the car.
They increase the collision time interval, thereby significantly reducing the average impact force experienced by the passenger.
They eliminate all kinetic energy instantly.

questions.q: A block is sliding down a rough inclined plane at a constant velocity. Which of the following statements is true?
a: The component of weight down the plane is less than the frictional force.
The normal contact force is zero.
There is a net down-slope accelerating force.
The component of weight down the plane is exactly balanced by the frictional force.
